svg.text: The migration pattern toolkit
Strangler Fig
Route requests at a facade/gateway: send extracted
capabilities to new services, the rest to the monolith,
until it's fully replaced. The default overall strategy.
Best when you can intercept traffic at the edge.
Branch by Abstraction
For seams DEEP in the code you can't route around:
introduce an abstraction (interface), build the new
implementation behind it, switch over, delete the old.
Lets you refactor safely without a long-lived branch.
Parallel Run
Run old and new implementations side by side on the
same input and COMPARE outputs (new one's result is
not yet used). Builds confidence before cutover.
Best for high-risk / correctness-critical extractions.
Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
A translation layer between the new service and the old
monolith model, so the monolith's legacy concepts don't
leak into and corrupt the new clean design (DDD).
Use whenever integrating with the legacy model.
Feature Toggle / Flag
Switch traffic between old and new paths with a config
flag — enabling canary %s and INSTANT rollback if the
new service misbehaves. The safety switch for cutover.
Change Data Capture / Events
Stream the monolith's data changes (from its DB log)
to keep the new service's data in sync — or to trigger
new behavior — without modifying the monolith's code.
